quran.note: The mother is inspired to suckle him and then cast him into the river; the family of Pharaoh pick him up; Pharaoh’s wife asks that he not be killed; his sister watches; he is returned to his mother.
Judgement and knowledge are given to him; he strikes down a man in the city, regrets it, and leaves in fear.
Madyan: he waters the flocks of two women, then is hired and offered a marriage on a term of service.
The fire, the call “O Moses”, the sacred valley of Tuwa, and “I am Allah. There is no deity except Me.”
His prayer: expand my breast, ease my task, untie the knot from my tongue, and give me Aaron my brother as a helper.
The two hosts see one another; he is told to strike the sea with his staff and it parts.
The path through the sea, and Pharaoh’s pursuit.
The forty nights, the calf taken for worship in his absence, and forgiveness.
Allah tells him his people have been led astray by the Samiri; he returns angry and grieved; Harun’s warning to the people.
Musa questions Harun and the Samiri; the calf is destroyed; “Your god is only Allah.”
He asks to see his Lord; the mountain crumbles; he is given the tablets.
He sets out with his servant for the meeting of the two seas and finds a servant of Allah given knowledge from Him.
The three events he cannot be patient about: the ship, the boy, the wall, and what lay behind each.
Believers are told not to be like those who abused Musa, and Allah cleared him of what they said.

hadith.summary: The Prophet ﷺ said Musa was very modest and kept his body fully covered, and some of the Children of Israel said it must be because of a defect in his skin. When he was bathing alone and a stone carried off his clothes, he ran after it naked, and they saw he was free of any defect.

After the Prophet ﷺ divided some goods, a man said the division had not been made for Allah’s sake. The Prophet ﷺ became visibly upset and asked Allah’s mercy on Musa, who had been hurt more than this and had been patient.

The Prophet ﷺ related that when the angel of death came to Musa, Musa struck him in the eye, and the angel went back to Allah. He was told to offer Musa a life extended by a year for every hair his hand covered on the back of an ox; Musa asked for death to come after that, and asked to be brought near the Holy Land, within a stone’s throw. The Prophet ﷺ said that if he were there he would show them the grave by the road, below the red sand hill.

A Muslim and a Jew each swore by the prophet he held highest, and the Muslim struck the Jew. The Prophet ﷺ said not to give him preference over Musa: on the Day of Resurrection people will fall unconscious, and he will find Musa holding a side of the Throne, not knowing whether Musa had fainted and been raised before him or was among those Allah exempted.

The Prophet ﷺ related that Musa told Adam his error had put him out of Paradise, and Adam answered that Allah had chosen Musa for His message and for speaking to him directly, and asked if Musa blamed him for what was decreed before he was created. The Prophet ﷺ said Adam won the argument.

hadith.narrator: Sa’id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka’b
hadith.summary: The long report of Musa and al-Khidr. Musa was rebuked for saying he was the most knowledgeable and told of a servant of Allah at the meeting of the two seas who knew more. He set out with his servant Yusha’ ibn Nun, met al-Khidr and asked to learn from him; al-Khidr warned that he would not be able to be patient, and Musa objected to three of his actions before they parted. The Prophet ﷺ said he wished Musa had been patient so that more of their story would have been told, and prayed for mercy on Musa.

When the Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah and saw the Jews fasting on Ashura, they said it was a good day on which Allah rescued the Children of Israel from their enemy, and Musa fasted it. The Prophet ﷺ said he had more claim to Musa than they did, fasted it, and told the Muslims to fast it.

In the Prophet’s ﷺ account of the night journey, Musa is the prophet in the sixth heaven. He welcomed the Prophet ﷺ as a brother and a prophet, and wept as he passed, saying that a youth sent after him would have more of his followers enter Paradise than Musa’s own.

When Allah first prescribed fifty prayers, Musa asked the Prophet ﷺ what had been enjoined, told him his people could not bear it, and kept sending him back to ask for a reduction until five remained. The Prophet ﷺ said he was too shy to ask again, and was told the five carry the reward of fifty.
hadith.note: This report is also given under Adam, where its different placement of Ibrahim is noted.

scholarly.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com)
scholarly.author: Ibn Kathir
scholarly.summary: Says that “you will not see Me” does not mean seeing Allah will never happen. He rejects the Mu’tazila on this, points to the mutawatir hadiths that believers will see Allah in the Hereafter (to be discussed under 75:22-23), and notes a report in earlier Scriptures that no living soul sees Allah and survives.

scholarly.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com)
scholarly.author: Ibn Kathir
scholarly.summary: Quotes a report from Anas ibn Malik (Musnad Ahmad) in which the Prophet ﷺ, explaining this verse, held out the tip of his little finger to show how little appeared to the mountain. Ibn Kathir says al-Tirmidhi recorded it and called it hasan sahih gharib, and that al-Hakim called it sahih on the standard of Muslim. We have not checked this report ourselves, so it is not listed with the verified hadith.

scholarly.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com)
scholarly.author: Ibn Kathir
scholarly.summary: On the Samiri and the “handful from the track of the messenger”: records Mujahid’s saying that the handful was taken from under the hoof of Jibril’s horse and says this is the well-known view of most tafsir scholars. It records Mujahid that what he threw on the jewellery became a calf’s body that made a sound, and that the sound came from the wind blowing through it. The abridged text does not assess the reliability of these reports.

scholarly.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com)
scholarly.author: Ibn Kathir
scholarly.summary: Says the servant of Allah was al-Khidr, relying on the authentic hadiths including the report of Ubayy ibn Ka’b in al-Bukhari through Sa’id ibn Jubayr. It names Musa’s servant as Yusha’ ibn Nun and mentions a spring at the meeting place called ‘Ayn al-Hayat. It does not say whether al-Khidr was a prophet, a wali or something else.

scholarly.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com)
scholarly.author: Ibn Kathir
scholarly.summary: Does not name the old man of Madyan. Records that the daughter, asked why she called Musa strong and trustworthy, said he had lifted a rock that took ten men and had told her to walk behind him; this is attributed to Umar, Ibn Abbas, Shurayh al-Qadi, Abu Malik, Qatadah, Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others. It also records from Sa’id ibn Jubayr (in al-Bukhari) that Ibn Abbas said Musa completed the longer and better of the two terms.

differences.question: What does “I am the first of the believers” mean (7:143)?

views.who: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid, preferred by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari
views.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com)
views.view: The first of the Children of Israel to believe.

views.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com)
views.view: That no one will see Allah in this life.

differences.question: Where was the Samiri from (20:95-96)?

views.who: Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Ibn Abbas
views.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com)
views.view: From the people of Bajarma, who worshipped cows; he outwardly accepted Islam with the Children of Israel while still loving cow worship, and his name was Musa ibn Zafar.

views.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com)

differences.note: The Qur’an gives only the name “the Samiri”.

differences.question: Was the Musa who met al-Khidr the prophet of the Children of Israel (18:60)?

views.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com)
views.view: He claimed that the Musa of al-Khidr was not the Musa of the Children of Israel.

views.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com)
views.view: He rejected this claim and called it a lie; his answer opens the report in Sahih al-Bukhari 3401.
